NeuralNg LoadingOverlay rules

- Import canonical `NeuralLoadingOverlay` only from `@neural-ng/core/loading-overlay`; `LoadingOverlayComponent` is a deprecated alias.
- Import canonical `NeuralLoadingIndicator` from the same entry point only when a custom indicator template is used; `LoadingIndicatorDirective` is a deprecated alias.
- Add imported standalone declarations directly to component imports.
- LoadingOverlay owns blocking, backdrop, timing, focus, and scroll behavior; ProgressSpinner owns only the visual indeterminate indicator.
- Container scope wraps and blocks only projected content.
- Viewport scope uses native dialog top-layer behavior and can lock document scroll.
- Bind active to application state; do not imperatively remove overlay DOM.
- Provide a task-specific label when "Loading" is not sufficient.
- The label defaults to the active locale common loading message.
- delay defaults to 150ms and prevents short-operation flashes.
- minimumDuration defaults to 300ms and prevents visible flicker.
- aria-busy begins immediately, even while visual rendering is delayed.
- blockInteraction defaults to true. Set it false only when continued interaction is safe.
- Escape never dismisses a loading operation.
- Do not create a close button or dismissible backdrop.
- Use spinnerSize and spinnerSeverity for the built-in ProgressSpinner.
- Use `<ng-template neuralLoadingIndicator>` for a custom indicator.
- Custom indicators receive polite status semantics; avoid duplicate live regions.
- `unstyled` removes visual classes while blocking and structural behavior remain.
- Slots: root, content, backdrop, panel, indicator, label.
- Global unstyled mode is `provideNeuralNg({ unstyled: true })`.
